It is an epithet of a swift river

where the scholiast is right: τὸν Ἀράξην, παρὰ τὸ ἀράσσειν καὶ ἠχεῖν τὰ κύματα αὐτοῦ [the Araxes, from the dashing and roaring of its waves]. Blomfield compared similar words of Herodotus about the river Gyndes 1, 189: κάρτα τε δὴ ἐχαλέπαινε τῷ ποταμῷ ὁ Κύρος͵ τούτῳ ὑβρίσαντι [Cyrus was very angry with the river, which had been insolent to him]. Add ποταμὸν ἀλαζόνα [a boastful river] said by Themistius or. 18 p. 221 d: Κροῖσος χρυσοῦ ψήγμασιν ἐκαλλωπίζετο, ἃ οὐχ ἡ γῆ αὐτῷ ἐδωροφόρει, ἀλλὰ ποταμὸς ἀλαζών [Croesus adorned himself with gold dust, which the earth did not bring him as a gift, but a boastful river did]. But it is strange that in Aeschylus's words the name of the river is not mentioned; since this is hardly probable, Hermann conjectured that one verse has fallen out after these words, such as σμερδνοῖς Ἀράξην κύμασιν βρυχώμενον [the Araxes roaring with terrible waves].
